name: 王可
objective:
本課程透過希臘英雄的偉大冒險故事以及希伯來聖經傳統中的聖哲事蹟來探索早期西方文明的兩大源頭（希臘與希伯來文化）所呈現出的主要風貌。
The main features of two great sources of early western civilizations, that is (1) Greek mythology and tragedies, and (2) Hebrew Biblical tradition, will be introduced to the students in the most exciting stories about Greek heroes and heroines as well as Biblical figures and events.
schedule:
This course introduces Western literature as both a tradition to study and a category to question. We will read influential works that have inspired a lineage of later writers while examining the works that have been forgotten in this tradition. Students are invited to practice critical thinking, make connections across texts and cultures, and develop the confidence to discuss complex ideas in English.

This is a rigorous and intellectually demanding course. Students are expected
to give their best effort at contributing to our community as a classroom, from partner work and class discussions to group projects. Students are also expected to do all readings, participate actively, listen respectfully, and take risks in developing their own interpretations. By the end of the semester, students will be better able to analyze literary language and connect texts to broader cultural and historical questions.
scorePolicy: Students will be strongly discouraged from using generative AI as a shortcut for language production, critical thinking, and independent projects. AI should never become a substitute for your own voice or judgment. This course is a place to practice discovering ideas and making choices for yourself, which matters more than quickly generating smooth (and ultimately lifeless) English.
